primary_diagnosis_treated: Stable atherosclerotic coronary artery disease post‑NSTEMI with stage 4 CKD, type 2 diabetes and hypertension
nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (Ischemic heart disease) ; NG203 (Chronic kidney disease) ; NG106 (Heart failure) ; TA902/TA929 (SGLT2‑i for CKD/HF)

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events after NSTEMI
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends lifelong aspirin 75 mg for all patients with established IHD

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce non‑HDL‑C by ≥40 % and lower CV risk in secondary prevention
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 advises high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all IHD patients

medications.dose: Start 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — renal function & K⁺ at 2 weeks after each change, then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Cardioprotective and renoprotective therapy for IHD, diabetes and CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 and NG203 recommend ACE‑I for IHD with hypertension/CKD; titration per guideline

medications.dose: Start 1.25 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5 mg (target HR 55‑60 bpm)
medications.duration: Lifelong — heart rate and BP review at each titration, then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Symptom control of angina and mortality reduction in IHD
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists cardio‑selective β‑blocker as first‑line anti‑anginal for IHD

medications.duration: Lifelong — renal function & electrolytes at 2 weeks, then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Renal protection and CV risk reduction in CKD stage 4 and secondary prevention after MI
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 and TA902/TA929 recommend dapagliflozin 10 mg for CKD (eGFR ≥25) and for post‑ACS secondary prevention

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in heart failure and can cause bradycardia when combined with β‑blocker
contraindications.alternative: Amlodipine if calcium‑channel blockade is required

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated with heart failure and β‑blocker use
Can worsen CKD and increase cardiovascular risk
Fluid retention and risk of heart failure in CKD
contraindications.alternative: Consider GLP‑1 receptor agonist if additional glucose lowering needed

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis when eGFR is in stage 4
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or DPP‑4 inhibitor with renal dosing

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
contraindications.alternative: Use ACE‑I alone; switch to ARB only if ACE‑I intolerant

assumptions_warnings: Exact eGFR not provided – assumed stage 4 CKD (eGFR ≈20‑30 ml/min/1.73 m²) for dosing decisions
Serum potassium and ACR not available – ACE‑I and potential MRA initiation require K⁺ ≤5.0 mmol/L and ACR ≥30 mg/mmol
Liver function tests not available – required before starting high‑intensity atorvastatin
Allergy status unknown – verify no aspirin, ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing
Platelet count 104 ×10³/µL (mild thrombocytopenia) – aspirin considered acceptable but monitor for bleeding
treatment_summary: Initiate guideline‑concordant secondary prevention for post‑NSTEMI: lifelong low‑dose aspirin, high‑intensity atorvastatin, ACE‑I (ramipril) and cardio‑selective β‑blocker (bisoprolol) with careful titration, and dapagliflozin for renal and cardiovascular protection. Avoid contraindicated agents (verapamil, diltiazem, chronic NSAIDs, pioglitazone, metformin in advanced CKD, ACE‑I + ARB). Obtain missing labs (eGFR, potassium, ACR, LFTs) and allergy history before finalising doses. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, blood pressure, heart rate and lipid profile as per NICE recommendations.
